arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ethan Davis argued the Hobbs Act requires obtaining property from another person.
Davis stated Ocasio was charged with taking property from the owners themselves.
Davis claimed the plain language of the statute resolves the case in his favor.
Davis argued a unity of purpose obscures the requirement to take from another.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Ocasio faces charges for conspiring with repair shop owners. The government claims this violates the Hobbs Act. Ocasio argues the law requires taking property from a third party.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Ocasio wants the conviction overturned because the law requires taking property from a third party.
The United States wants the conviction upheld because the conspiracy satisfied all statutory elements.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Ocasio argues the plain language of the Hobbs Act requires obtaining property from another person.
The United States argues a conspiracy to commit an offense satisfies the statute even if the victim is a co-conspirator.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of federal extortion laws. It clarifies who qualifies as a victim under the statute. The outcome shapes how prosecutors charge conspiracy cases involving property owners.
